title: Explainable quantization decision heuristics and per-model defaults
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: produce a deterministic, explainable decision layer that selects a recommended quantization profile (FP8/INT8/FP16) for each model variant in the catalog, plus a concise guardrail set and an automatic fallback chain. This work focuses on: (1) the decision heuristics (latency/cost/accuracy trade-offs), (2) an explainability signature attached to each recommendation (what tests were used and why), and (3) integration points for telemetry-driven re-tuning.

Why: Customers and internal reviewers need to understand why a model was recommended for INT8 vs FP8, what calibration data influenced the choice, and what automatic fallbacks will occur when telemetry signals quality regressions. Current catalog entries list allowed quant modes but lack a transparent decision story and runtime telemetry hooks.

Scope: implement a decision heuristic microservice and catalogue metadata fields, add a per-model "explainability signature" (small JSON blob persisted in the catalog entry), and a short-list of calibration artifacts needed to validate the recommendation. Deliverables: (A) API to compute recommendation and signature, (B) migration of three pilot models (open-llama-7b, rw-crypto-13b, rw-instruct-3b) to include recommendations, (C) dashboard panels showing telemetry signals mapped to recommendation triggers, (D) CI gating checks that prevent shipping a recommendation without passing a lightweight calibration validation and CI signature.

Non-goals: end-to-end automatic re-quantization in production (will be a follow-up), full retraining of quant-aware models, or support for exotic numeric formats beyond FP8/INT8/FP16.
acceptance_criteria: 1) API returns a recommended profile and an explainability signature for a model in < 200ms for cached results; 2) signature includes: dataset used for calibration, L2/accuracy delta metrics vs baseline, kernel compatibility hints, and fallback chain; 3) Pilot models show <= 2% degradation in core eval slices for INT8 recommendations, or a documented reason and fallback to FP8; 4) Catalog UI displays the recommendation and a 'Why' link to the signature; 5) CI gate rejects PRs that add recommendations without attached calibration artifact links.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (internal pilot): enable recommendation API behind feature flag and surface signatures for 3 pilot models in staging console (1 week). Phase 2 (limited customers): open recommendations to early access customers and record telemetry for 30 days (3 weeks). Phase 3 (catalog-wide rollout): run batch inference validation across catalog subset and push recommendations with audit log and opt-out controls (2 weeks). Emergency rollback: feature flag + catalog tombstone field to revert to explicit 'no-recommendation' entries.

Observability: add metrics for recommendation request rate, compute time, mismatches between recommended profile and runtime used, and quality regression alerts tied to telemetry thresholds defined in the design doc.
test_plan: Unit tests for decision heuristics, property tests for signature contents, integration test that validates calibration artifacts (run small calibration harness with 512-example sample), and e2e test that simulates a telemetry-driven fall-forward: degrade a model with synthetic noise and assert the system surfaces a fallback in the UI within defined SLAs. Add CI job 'quant-recommendation-smoke' that runs on PRs modifying catalog metadata. Reference PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-catalog/pull/1297. Calibration doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Sample-Limited+Calibration+Guidelines.
notes:
Design trade-offs discussed: (a) heavy-weight calibration (full eval) vs lightweight sample-limited calibration — we choose lightweight for catalog speed but require conservative guardrails; (b) opaque ML-driven recommenders vs rule-first heuristics — we chose a hybrid: rules encode hard safety constraints (e.g., >X tokens/s latency targets) and a small learned model ranks safe profiles; (c) storage: store a compact explainability signature (not raw calibration data) to keep catalog small.

Open questions: what is the canonical calibration dataset per model? (proposal: dataset subset + representative prompt buckets stored as artifact links). How to version signatures when model weights change? Answer: signatures are tied to model version and invalidated on new weights.

Security notes: signatures may reference calibration data with customer-provided examples; ensure access control and audit logs. Coordinate with Security (ticket SEC-2143) on KMS for artifact access where needed.
